paper_cards.title: RoboWM-Bench: A Benchmark for Evaluating World Models in Robotic Manipulation
paper_cards.data: manipulation-centric benchmark that turns generated human-hand and robotic manipulation videos into embodied action sequences and validates them through execution in standardized manipulation scenarios
paper_cards.method: convert generated behaviors into executable action sequences, replay them in a robotics execution loop, and score physically executable task completion with failure-mode analysis
paper_cards.task: evaluate whether video world-model predictions can be translated into executable manipulation actions that still complete the intended task
paper_cards.novelty: moves world-model evaluation from visual plausibility to embodiment-grounded action executability for robotic manipulation
paper_cards.evidence: Primary evidence from CVPRW + arXiv + official GitHub; benchmark scale, task framing, and release status were traced to official or primary sources.

claim_checks.claim: Manipulation benchmark converts generated behaviors into embodied action sequences and validates them through execution.
claim_checks.notes: CVPRW abstract states execution-grounded conversion and validation.

claim_checks.claim: Benchmark exposes failure modes in spatial reasoning, contact prediction, and deformation.
claim_checks.notes: Primary abstract lists these persistent failure modes.

claim_checks.claim: Official code is public.
claim_checks.notes: Public GitHub repository exists.

paper_cards.limitations: Workshop-paper scope is narrower than broader cross-domain world-model benchmarks, and the benchmark is centered on manipulation rather than navigation or open-domain interaction.
paper_cards.project_relevance: Direct benchmark reference for whether generated embodied futures are actionable enough for manipulation-policy learning and validation.

paper_cards.title: VLA-Arena: An Open-Source Framework for Benchmarking Vision-Language-Action Models
paper_cards.data: 170 tasks across 11 specialized suites with three difficulty levels, plus VLA-Arena-S/M/L datasets and orthogonal language and visual perturbation settings
paper_cards.method: structured benchmark design over task structure, language command, and visual observation axes with unified tooling for task modeling, training, and automated evaluation
paper_cards.task: systematically benchmark VLA robustness, safety, extrapolation, distractor handling, and long-horizon composition under controlled perturbations
paper_cards.novelty: separates VLA capability-frontier measurement into orthogonal structure/language/visual axes instead of collapsing everything into one aggregate success rate
paper_cards.evidence: Primary evidence from arXiv + project + official GitHub; benchmark scale, task framing, and release status were traced to official or primary sources.

claim_checks.claim: VLA-Arena defines 170 tasks grouped into Safety, Distractor, Extrapolation, and Long Horizon dimensions.
claim_checks.notes: arXiv abstract states the 170-task structure and four dimensions.

claim_checks.claim: The benchmark uses orthogonal language and visual perturbations and ships datasets/framework/leaderboard.
claim_checks.notes: Primary abstract and project links state W0-W4, V0-V4, datasets, and leaderboard.

claim_checks.claim: Official open-source framework is public.
claim_checks.notes: GitHub repo contains toolchain and task suites.

paper_cards.limitations: It is simulator-centric and VLA-specific, so it does not directly evaluate world-model video rollouts or open-domain interactive generation.
paper_cards.project_relevance: Strong infrastructure reference for evaluation schemas, perturbation taxonomies, and task-difficulty ladders for embodied policy assessment.

paper_cards.title: Colosseum V2: Benchmarking Generalization for Vision Language Action Models
paper_cards.data: large-scale ManiSkill benchmark with 28 tasks spanning 13 categories, two robot morphologies, and controlled in-domain/out-of-domain perturbation settings
paper_cards.method: GPU-parallelized simulation benchmark that probes VLA generalization along visual, language, and action axes and checks ecological validity against real-world metrics
paper_cards.task: measure how VLA manipulation performance degrades under distribution shift and whether simulation rankings track real-world robustness
paper_cards.novelty: pushes VLA evaluation beyond nominal zero-shot perception into controlled perturbation-based generalization measurement with simulation-to-real correlation checks
paper_cards.evidence: Primary evidence from arXiv HTML/abs; benchmark scale, task framing, and release status were traced to official or primary sources.

claim_checks.claim: Benchmark contains 28 tasks across 13 categories and two robot morphologies.
claim_checks.notes: Primary abstract states the scale and structure.

claim_checks.claim: Built on ManiSkill with fast GPU-parallelized evaluation and in-domain/out-of-domain testing.
claim_checks.notes: Primary abstract and HTML page describe the simulator and testing regime.

claim_checks.claim: Simulation metrics correlate with real-world metrics.
claim_checks.notes: Primary abstract explicitly claims strong correlation.

paper_cards.limitations: No clearly surfaced official public code release was confirmed during this run, and current evidence comes mainly from the arXiv paper page.
paper_cards.project_relevance: Useful benchmark template for large-scale, perturbation-aware embodied policy evaluation and simulation-to-real validation.

paper_cards.title: MiraBench: Evaluating Action-Conditioned Reliability in Robotic World Models
paper_cards.data: human-annotated corpus with 16k+ judgments covering tasks, failure categories, and 12 representative robotic-world-model configurations
paper_cards.method: hierarchical diagnostic benchmark over physics adherence, action-following fidelity, and optimism-bias detection for action-conditioned robotic world models
paper_cards.task: test whether action-conditioned robotic world models are physically consistent, obey task-relevant actions, and avoid optimistic false-success predictions
paper_cards.novelty: defines action-conditioned reliability as a first-class target rather than assuming image fidelity stands in for robotic faithfulness
paper_cards.evidence: Primary evidence from arXiv; benchmark scale, task framing, and release status were traced to official or primary sources.

claim_checks.claim: Benchmark is decomposed into Physics Adherence, Action-Following Fidelity, and Optimism Bias Detection.
claim_checks.notes: Explicit in the abstract.

claim_checks.claim: Corpus contains over 16,000 judgments and evaluates 12 representative model configurations.
claim_checks.notes: Primary abstract provides these counts.

claim_checks.claim: Visual fidelity is a poor proxy for action fidelity.
claim_checks.notes: Primary abstract reports this as a central finding.

paper_cards.limitations: Public project/code artifacts were not clearly surfaced during this run, so reproducibility signals are weaker than the best open benchmark releases.
paper_cards.project_relevance: Directly relevant to evaluating whether generated futures are faithful control simulators rather than merely plausible videos.

paper_cards.title: iWorld-Bench: A Benchmark for Interactive World Models with a Unified Action Generation Framework
paper_cards.data: 330k video clips, 2.1k selected high-quality samples, and 4.9k test tasks spanning varied perspectives, weather, and scenes
paper_cards.method: unified action-generation framework that standardizes interaction control across modalities and scores world models on visual generation, trajectory following, and memory with nine metrics
paper_cards.task: train and test interactive world models on distance perception, action control, camera control, trajectory following, and memory across diverse scenes
paper_cards.novelty: turns interactive world-model evaluation into a multi-input, action-space-unified benchmark instead of model-specific camera-control demos
paper_cards.evidence: Primary evidence from ICML project page + arXiv + official GitHub; benchmark scale, task framing, and release status were traced to official or primary sources.

claim_checks.claim: Project reports 330K video clips, 2.1K selected samples, and 4.9K test tasks.
claim_checks.notes: Official project page exposes these counts.

claim_checks.claim: Benchmark evaluates interactive world models across multiple inputs, action control, camera control, memory, and all-weather settings.
claim_checks.notes: Comparison table on official project page states the capability coverage.

claim_checks.claim: Official code and dataset are public.
claim_checks.notes: GitHub repository and dataset links are public.

paper_cards.limitations: The current release is centered on interactive video-generation style world models rather than manipulation-policy world models, so mapping to robotics execution still requires care.
paper_cards.project_relevance: High-value benchmark for first-person interactive world-model evaluation, camera control, memory, and multi-scene action responsiveness.

paper_cards.title: WBench: A Comprehensive Multi-turn Benchmark for Interactive Video World Model Evaluation
paper_cards.data: 289 multi-turn test cases and 1,058 interaction turns covering navigation, subject action, event editing, and perspective switching
paper_cards.method: comprehensive multi-turn benchmark with 22 automatic sub-metrics across video quality, setting adherence, interaction adherence, consistency, and physics compliance
paper_cards.task: evaluate whether interactive video world models sustain coherent multi-turn behavior under heterogeneous control interfaces
paper_cards.novelty: brings multi-turn interaction and heterogeneous control-interface unification into one benchmark rather than one-step or single-axis evaluation
paper_cards.evidence: Primary evidence from arXiv + official homepage + official GitHub; benchmark scale, task framing, and release status were traced to official or primary sources.

claim_checks.claim: Benchmark has 289 test cases and 1,058 interaction turns across five evaluation dimensions.
claim_checks.notes: Primary abstract provides these counts and dimensions.

claim_checks.claim: Official repo evaluates 22 video world models across 22 metrics.
claim_checks.notes: Official GitHub README states the current leaderboard scale and metrics.

claim_checks.claim: Official code/data site is public.
claim_checks.notes: Public GitHub repo and homepage exist.

paper_cards.limitations: The benchmark is tilted toward interactive video-world-model families rather than physically executable robot-control environments.
paper_cards.project_relevance: Strong benchmark reference for multi-turn interaction fidelity and physics-compliance evaluation in interactive world generation.

paper_cards.title: WorldMark: A Unified Benchmark Suite for Interactive Video World Models
paper_cards.data: 500 standardized evaluation cases built from 100 test images and 15 shared action sequences across first-person, third-person, real, and stylized scenes
paper_cards.method: shared WASD-style action vocabulary, cross-model action mapping, and modular metrics for visual quality, control alignment, and world consistency, paired with the World Model Arena website
paper_cards.task: compare interactive image-to-video world models under identical scenes and identical action sequences
paper_cards.novelty: creates the first common playing field for interactive image-to-video world models with standardized scenes, controls, and reusable evaluation toolkit
paper_cards.evidence: Primary evidence from arXiv + official project + World Model Arena; benchmark scale, task framing, and release status were traced to official or primary sources.

claim_checks.claim: WorldMark provides 500 evaluation cases built from 100 test images and 15 standardized action sequences.
claim_checks.notes: Official project page gives the image/action suite counts.

claim_checks.claim: Benchmark evaluates visual quality, control alignment, and world consistency with eight metrics.
claim_checks.notes: Official results section lists the metrics.

claim_checks.claim: World Model Arena provides a live leaderboard and side-by-side battles.
claim_checks.notes: Official arena page exposes leaderboard and voting workflow.

paper_cards.limitations: Current emphasis is on interactive image-to-video world models rather than embodied robot execution, and code is surfaced mainly through the project site rather than a standalone repo.
paper_cards.project_relevance: Important benchmark and online-comparison reference for standardized interactive world-generation evaluation.

paper_cards.title: WorldOlympiad: Can Your World Model Survive a Triathlon?
paper_cards.data: 1,000 long videos spanning 400 robotics, 400 gaming, and 200 general real-world videos
paper_cards.method: triathlon-style benchmark with physical, geometry, and interaction tracks using segmentation-based judges, Gaussian-splatting diagnostics, and action-following checks
paper_cards.task: diagnose long-video world models on physical faithfulness, geometric consistency, and interaction fidelity across multiple downstream domains
paper_cards.novelty: unifies physical, geometric, and interaction diagnostics across robotics, gaming, and open-domain world-model scenarios rather than isolating one dimension
paper_cards.evidence: Primary evidence from arXiv + official project + official GitHub; benchmark scale, task framing, and release status were traced to official or primary sources.

claim_checks.claim: Benchmark covers physical, geometric, and interactive tracks.
claim_checks.notes: Official repo/project states the triathlon decomposition.

claim_checks.claim: Dataset contains 1,000 long videos including 400 robotics videos.
claim_checks.notes: Official repository overview lists the domain split.

claim_checks.claim: Official repository is public.
claim_checks.notes: Public GitHub repo exists.

paper_cards.limitations: Because it spans robotics, gaming, and general video, some metrics are less tightly aligned to embodied manipulation than manipulation-specific benchmarks.
paper_cards.project_relevance: Strong cross-domain benchmark for long-horizon world-model evaluation with direct relevance to robotics and interactive control.

paper_cards.title: WorldBench: Disambiguating Physics for Diagnostic Evaluation of World Models
paper_cards.data: video benchmark with 425 configurations over motion physics, object permanence, support relations, and scale/perspective, plus a language subset for VLM evaluation
paper_cards.method: disentangled physics benchmark that scores future predictions against simulated ground-truth physical outcomes using segmentation-based comparison and concept-specific scenarios
paper_cards.task: diagnose whether world models and VLMs understand specific physical concepts rather than merely producing visually plausible futures
paper_cards.novelty: disentangles physical concepts into more diagnostic tests instead of entangled holistic video-quality proxies
paper_cards.evidence: Primary evidence from arXiv + official project; benchmark scale, task framing, and release status were traced to official or primary sources.

claim_checks.claim: WorldBench covers 425 configurations across four physically rich scenarios.
claim_checks.notes: Official project page gives the configuration count and scenarios.

claim_checks.claim: Benchmark directly evaluates world-model video prediction against simulated physical outcomes.
claim_checks.notes: Project overview explains the evaluation loop.

claim_checks.claim: All tested configurations still lack sufficient physical consistency.
claim_checks.notes: Official abstract/results say current models fall short.

paper_cards.limitations: It is more physics-diagnostic than interaction- or policy-oriented, so it complements but does not replace action-grounded embodied benchmarks.
paper_cards.project_relevance: Useful physics-diagnostic benchmark for checking whether world models preserve support, permanence, and motion rules relevant to executable embodied worlds.
